extra.message: The user-supplied search query `q` (from URL query string, schema allows any string) is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string (`WHERE name LIKE '%${query}%' OR description LIKE '%${query}%'`) that is executed via prisma.$queryRawUnsafe() (line 100). The only defense is a bypassable keyword blacklist (isSQLInjectionAttempt, lines 7-33), which does not block UNION-based payloads using case/encoding tricks or stacked queries via other syntax. This allows arbitrary SQL injection against the SQLite database (data exfiltration, auth bypass).

The user-supplied `status` field from the JSON body is interpolated directly into a raw SQL query: `WHERE o."userId" = '${user.id}' ${statusFilter}` where statusFilter (line 81) is `AND o.status = '${status}'`. Executed via prisma.$queryRawUnsafe (line 102). Only a bypassable keyword blacklist guards it, so an authenticated user can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g., UNION SELECT to read any table).

The X-Forwarded-For request header (line 58) is concatenated unescaped into an INSERT statement (`VALUES ('${id}', '${ip}', ...)`) executed via prisma.$queryRawUnsafe (line 103). This endpoint is unauthenticated and the header is fully attacker-controlled, enabling arbitrary SQL injection (e.g., stacked queries, subqueries via INSERT ... SELECT) into the visitor_logs table.

Second-order SQL injection: the review `author` field is stored un-sanitized (via POST /api/products/[id]/reviews where author is arbitrary user input), then interpolated directly into raw SQL (`WHERE r.author = '${authorFilter}'`, lines 113 and 133) executed with better-sqlite3 db.exec()/prepare().all(). An admin filtering by a crafted author name triggers SQL injection. Only a bypassable keyword blacklist (lines 10-36) filters the input.

User-supplied XML (request body) is parsed with libxmljs.parseXmlString(rawXml, { noent: true, dtdload: true }). `noent: true` enables entity substitution and `dtdload: true` allows loading external DTDs, so an XML payload with an external general entity (e.g., <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///flag-xxe.txt">) causes arbitrary local file read (and potentially network SSRF via SYSTEM URLs), with entity values reflected in the response.

The weak containsMaliciousContent blocklist (lines 19-29) checks only a few strings and is only used to award a flag — the malicious file is still saved (lines 83-85) and its URL stored on the product. cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

Server-Side Request Forgery: the unauthenticated support form accepts an arbitrary `screenshotUrl` which is fetched server-side with fetch(screenshotUrl) — no scheme, host, or IP validation, no allowlist. cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: Hardcoded weak JWT signing secret: `const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'secret'` — when the environment variable is unset the app signs and verifies all authentication tokens with the literal string 'secret'. An attacker who knows this (it is also hinted inside issued tokens: payload field hint = 'The secret is not so secret') can forge arbitrary HS256 tokens with role ADMIN and completely bypass authentication on all withAuth/withAdminAuth endpoints.

Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (hashMD5, used for signup at app/api/auth/signup/route.ts:46, login comparison at app/api/auth/login/route.ts:27/46, and password reset at app/api/auth/reset-password/route.ts:46). MD5 is cryptographically broken and trivially reversible via rainbow tables for typical passwords; combined with the SQL injection and data-export flaws, an attacker recovers all account passwords including the admin's.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: Predictable password reset token: the reset token is `hashMD5(email + timestamp)` — a deterministic MD5 over the victim's (known) email and a coarse Unix timestamp. The response also returns `requestedAt` (line 42), giving the attacker the exact timestamp window, so they can recompute the token offline and reset any account's password via POST /api/auth/reset-password. No cryptographic randomness is involved.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: Hardcoded fallback encryption key: SHARE_ENCRYPTION_KEY defaults to the literal hex string 'a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2' committed in source when SHARE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Tokens are the sole authorization for this unauthenticated endpoint, so forged tokens (e.g., 'report:internal' or 'order:<any id>') expose any user's order details and the internal security report.
